summary.prose: Building this Story means giving the VS Code chat's own direct Vibe launch path the same safety machinery the backend adapter already has: a per-turn export directory it owns, a dispatchState tracker that mirrors the adapter's model exactly, and a real exit classification read from Vibe's own export.json instead of a guess. That classification gets stamped onto the one durable marker both the live writer and a reattaching follower already consult, so a resumed turn is judged exactly as safely as a live one. Once that's proven, the Story deletes the old worker-routed path it replaces and gates the final cutover on a live approval-flag equivalence check.

epicImpact.reason: Story s3 mirrors contracts (dispatchState model, buildArgv's export-directory parameter) that Story s1 built and Story s2 later extended within the SAME file (src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts); must confirm s2's extension did not change what s3 mirrors.
epicImpact.findings: s1 built the shared adapter (src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts) including the dispatchState model ('not-sent'->'possibly-sent'->'accepted') and buildArgv's 2-argument export-directory contract that Story s3's alternative a1 mirrors inside cli-adapter.ts's direct-spawn vibe branch; s1's own t7 FAILED (disclosed, a repo-wide contract test gap, unrelated to s3's scope). s2 built the read-only qualification suite (ReadOnlyCapability, qualifyReadOnlyCapability, the now-renamed argvExcludingTurnLocalFlags) on top of the SAME vibe-adapter.ts file, but its changed-files list (confirmed via its own BUILD record) touches only src/shared/vibe-adapter.ts and src/agent/providers/cli-provider.ts -- no file under vscode-plugin/src/chat/ -- and none of s2's additions touch buildArgv's ordinary (non-read-only) argv construction or the ordinary dispatchState transitions s3 mirrors; its own disclosed Task failures (t4: non-self-triggering readOnly field; t7: amendment filed via a different Story's workflow) are both scoped to the read-only authorization path. No contradiction or re-work needed: s3 may proceed mirroring s1's original dispatchState/export-directory model exactly as the approved LLD describes, without any HLD back-flow for epic-state reasons.
